name: Swaps in Permutation
description: You are given a permutation of the numbers 1, 2, ..., n and m pairs of positions ( a j , b j ) . At each step you can choose a pair from the given positions and swap the numbers in that positions. What is the lexicographically maximal permutation one can get? Let p and q be two permutations of the numbers 1, 2, ..., n . p is lexicographically smaller than the q if a number 1 ≤ i ≤ n exists, so p k = q k for 1 ≤ k < i and p i < q i .
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and m ( 1 ≤ n , m ≤ 10 6 ) — the length of the permutation p and the number of pairs of positions. The second line contains n distinct integers p i ( 1 ≤ p i ≤ n ) — the elements of the permutation p . Each of the last m lines contains two integers ( a j , b j ) ( 1 ≤ a j , b j ≤ n ) — the pairs of positions to swap. Note that you are given a positions , not the values to swap.
output_specification: Print the only line with n distinct integers p ' i ( 1 ≤ p ' i ≤ n ) — the lexicographically maximal permutation one can get.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 691D — Swaps in Permutation [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
